Ava (Support): Customer on paid tier seeing intermittent 503s & spikes to 2.5s on POST /v1/generate. They only have timestamps: 2024-09-12T14:03:10Z -> 2024-09-12T14:07:00Z. No request-id shared. Can we get a minimal repro + the exact headers to ask them to capture?
Devon (SRE): Ask for a Request ID first (x-request-id header or X-Request-Id). If they didn't capture it we still can search traces by time window but request ids make it 10x faster. Also request they include response headers (we return x-request-id and x-server-latency-ms).
Ava (Support): Copying a tiny curl + what to paste back. Keep it short for customer.
Devon (SRE): Here's a compact curl they can run (replace KEY and PAYLOAD). It forces a request-id and prints headers + body:
```bash
curl -sS -D - \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_KEY>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Request-Id: customer-<your-id>" \
  --data '{"model":"rwd-1-large","input":"hello"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate --compressed
```
"Please copy the full HTTP response (status + headers) and the exact wall-clock time when they ran it."
Priya (Eng): If they prefer SDK snippets, share these minimal examples. They should run from a dev machine and paste back stdout/stderr + any request-id.
Priya (Eng): Python (requests)
```python
import requests
import time
url = "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate"
headers = {
  "Authorization": "Bearer <REDACTED_KEY>",
  "Content-Type": "application/json",
  "X-Request-Id": "customer-python-123"
}
payload = {"model":"rwd-1-large","input":"hello"}
start = time.time()
r = requests.post(url, json=payload, headers=headers, timeout=10)
print('status', r.status_code)
print('headers', dict(r.headers))
print('body', r.text[:1000])
print('elapsed', time.time()-start)
```
Priya (Eng): Node (fetch)
```js
const fetch = require('node-fetch')
(async ()=>{
  const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': 'Bearer <REDACTED_KEY>',
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      'X-Request-Id': 'customer-js-123'
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({model:'rwd-1-large', input:'hello'}),
    // optional: set timeout with AbortController if they want
  })
  console.log('status', res.status)
  res.headers.forEach((v,k)=> console.log(k, v))
  const text = await res.text()
  console.log('body', text.slice(0,1000))
})()
```
Priya (Eng): Go (net/http)
```go
package main
import (
  "bytes"
  "fmt"
  "net/http"
  "io/ioutil"
  "time"
)
func main(){
  client := &http.Client{Timeout: 10*time.Second}
  req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST","https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate", bytes.NewBufferString(`{"model":"rwd-1-large","input":"hello"}`))
  req.Header.Set("Authorization","Bearer <REDACTED_KEY>")
  req.Header.Set("Content-Type","application/json")
  req.Header.Set("X-Request-Id","customer-go-123")
  start := time.Now()
  resp, err := client.Do(req)
  fmt.Println("err", err)
  defer resp.Body.Close()
  b,_ := ioutil.ReadAll(resp.Body)
  fmt.Println("status", resp.StatusCode)
  fmt.Println("headers", resp.Header)
  fmt.Println("body", string(b)[:1000])
  fmt.Println("elapsed", time.Since(start))
}
```
Devon (SRE): Also ask them to enable SDK debug env var if they used an SDK (this prints request/response metadata): `REDWOOD_SDK_DEBUG=1` for one-shot runs, then paste logs.
